what_it_does: Running a large language model at scale involves two distinct phases: first processing the entire user prompt all at once (prefill), then generating the reply one word at a time (decode). Some systems split these two phases onto separate machines to avoid one slowing the other, but that separation introduces waiting time in queues. Other systems run both phases on the same machine, avoiding queue delays but letting the two phases compete for the chip's resources. Tropical proposes a middle path — a scheduler that dynamically assigns some machines to handle both phases together and others to handle only one, picking the mix in real time to keep both response-time targets (time until the first word appears, and time between subsequent words) within agreed limits. The key novelty is making this switching decision continuously based on live load rather than a fixed policy.
